sentences: A universal point set must support a crossing-free straight-line drawing of every planar graph with n vertices.
For each graph, its vertices may use a different subset of the same fixed points.
The question asks how small this common geometric host can be, especially whether a linear number of points suffices.
Rectangular grid drawings give a useful construction but impose additional structure on the host.
The target measures how much geometric freedom is needed to realize all planar combinatorial structures of one size.
